blocks.text: The chapter traces the glory of YHWH from the temple threshold to the cherubim and then to the east gate (vv. 18–19). Within Ezekiel’s larger vision, this movement is understood as part of the glory leaving the defiled temple and city in chapters 8–11, before its return to the visionary sanctuary in chapter 43. The repeated language of “appearance” and “likeness,” also used in Ezekiel’s earlier throne vision, signals that Ezekiel is describing a vision whose realities exceed straightforward visual description.
